Der Froschkönig oder der eiserne Heinrich
The Frog King, or Iron Henry

A princess drops her golden ball in a deep well. A frog fetches it if she will let him eat from her plate and sleep in her bed. She breaks her word, he comes to the castle anyway, and when she throws him at the wall in a temper he falls down a king's son. His servant Henry had bound his heart with three iron bands for grief, and they snap one by one for joy on the way home.
Der Wolf und die sieben jungen Geißlein
The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids

A mother goat warns her seven kids never to open the door to the wolf. He softens his voice with chalk and whitens his paw with flour, and gets in. Only the youngest, hidden in the clock case, is left to tell her, and together they get the others back safe.

A man steals rampion from an enchantress's garden for his wife, and pays with their child, Rapunzel, who is shut in a tower with no door. The enchantress climbs her long golden hair. A king's son learns the call, is found out, falls blind into thorns, and wanders for years until Rapunzel's tears heal his eyes.

A poor woodcutter's children are left in the forest. The first time Hansel's white pebbles lead them home; the second time the birds eat his breadcrumbs. They find a house of bread with a roof of cake and windows of sugar. Clever Gretel outwits the witch who lives there, frees her brother, and a white duck carries them home across the great water.
Von dem Fischer un syner Fru
The Fisherman and his Wife

A fisherman lets a magic flounder go. His wife sends him back to ask for a cottage, then a castle, then to be king, emperor and pope, and the sea grows darker and wilder each time. When she wants to be like God, they are back in their old hovel.

A girl made to sleep in the ashes plants a hazel twig on her mother's grave, and it grows into a tree where a white bird gives her what she wishes. The doves help her pick lentils from the ashes. Three nights she goes to the king's ball in gold and silver; on the third the prince has the stairs smeared with pitch, and her golden slipper sticks.

A girl falls down a well into a meadow. She takes the bread out of the oven when it calls, shakes the apple tree when it asks, and shakes Mother Holle's featherbed so that it snows on the world. She goes home under a gate that showers her with gold. Her lazy sister gets pitch.

A girl in a red velvet cap takes cake and wine to her grandmother, strays from the path to pick flowers, and the wolf gets there first. A huntsman saves them both. Another day she meets another wolf, keeps to the path, and with Grandmother tricks him off the roof into the trough.
Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten
The Bremen Town Musicians

An old donkey, dog, cat and rooster, no longer wanted, set out to be town musicians in Bremen. In the forest they find a robbers' house, stand on each other's backs at the window and sing all together, and the robbers run for their lives. They like the house so much they never get to Bremen.
The Elves and the Shoemaker

A poor shoemaker cuts out leather at night, and in the morning the shoes are made, perfectly. He and his wife watch and see two little naked men at work, so they sew them tiny clothes. The elves dress, dance out of the door, and never come back, but the shoemaker never wants again.

A thirteenth wise woman, not invited to the christening, curses the princess to prick her finger on a spindle and die. The twelfth softens it to a hundred years' sleep. The whole castle sleeps with her, down to the flies on the wall, and a hedge of thorns grows round it. On the day the hundred years end, the thorns turn to flowers and let a king's son through.

A queen asks her mirror who is the fairest in the land, and the answer is Snow White. The girl escapes to the seven dwarfs beyond the seven mountains. The queen comes three times, with laces, a comb and a poisoned apple. The dwarfs lay her in a glass coffin, and when the prince's servants stumble carrying it, the piece of apple falls from her throat.

A miller boasts that his daughter can spin straw into gold. Locked in with the straw, she is helped three nights by a little man, for her necklace, her ring and then her first child. As queen she has three days to guess his name. A messenger hears him singing it by his fire on the mountain.

The youngest son, whom everyone calls Simpleton, shares his food with a little grey man and finds a goose with golden feathers. Everyone who touches it sticks fast: three sisters, a parson, a sexton, two farmhands. The sight of them all makes a princess who has never laughed laugh.
Die zertanzten Schuhe
The Twelve Dancing Princesses

Every morning the twelve princesses' shoes are danced to pieces. An old soldier with a cloak that makes him unseen follows them through a trapdoor, past trees with leaves of silver, gold and diamond, over a lake in twelve boats, to a castle where they dance all night. He brings back a twig from each grove to prove it.
Das tapfere Schneiderlein
The Brave Little Tailor

A tailor kills seven flies at one blow and sews it on his belt. Everyone thinks he means seven men. He tricks two giants into fighting each other by dropping stones on them as they sleep, catches a unicorn and a wild boar, and wins a kingdom.
Tischchen deck dich, Goldesel und Knüppel aus dem Sack
The Wishing-Table, the Gold-Donkey and the Cudgel in the Sack
Three brothers are given a table that lays itself, a donkey that drops gold, and a cudgel that jumps out of its sack. A greedy innkeeper steals the first two, until the cudgel gets them back.

A poor girl is given a little pot. Say 'Cook, little pot, cook' and it makes sweet millet porridge; say 'Stop, little pot' and it stops. Her mother forgets the words, and the porridge fills the kitchen, the house, the street and the town.
Der goldene Schlüssel

In winter a poor boy digs in the snow for wood and finds a little golden key. Where there is a key there must be a lock, he thinks, and digs again, and finds an iron casket. He turns the key once round. 'Now we must wait until he has quite unlocked it and lifted the lid, and then we shall learn what wonderful things were in the casket.' It is the last tale in the book.
Märchen von einem, der auszog, das Fürchten zu lernen
The Boy Who Went Forth to Learn What Fear Was

A boy who cannot shudder spends three nights in a haunted castle, plays skittles with dead men's bones, and is not afraid at all. He only learns to shudder when his wife pours a bucket of cold water full of little fishes over him in bed.
Der treue Johannes
A king's youngest son follows a fox's advice (mostly) to win a golden bird, a golden horse and the princess of the golden castle.

Jacob Grimm (1785-1863) and Wilhelm Grimm (1786-1859) grew up in Hanau and Steinau in Hesse. Their father died when they were boys and the family was poor. They studied law at Marburg, where their teacher Savigny showed them his library of old German books, and they fell in love with the past.
Which was the older brother?
Collecting the tales

From 1806 the brothers wrote down tales told by people they knew in Kassel: the Wild family, the Hassenpflug sisters, the von Haxthausens, and an old soldier, Johann Krause, who traded tales for their old trousers. They believed these tales kept the oldest poetry of the German people.
Where did the brothers write down most of the tales?

Their finest storyteller was Dorothea Viehmann (1755-1815), a tailor's wife from Niederzwehren near Kassel, daughter of the innkeeper of the Knallhütte. She told them about forty tales, word for word the same each time, and slowly so they could write. Her picture is in the second volume.
What did Dorothea Viehmann do to help the brothers write?
Told each tale the same each time, slowly
Wrote the tales herself
Sang them as songs
The first edition, 1812
Kinder- und Hausmärchen (Children's and Household Tales) came out at Christmas 1812 with 86 tales; a second volume of 70 followed in 1815. It had no pictures and long scholarly notes. It sold slowly.
How many tales were in the first volume of 1812?

Wilhelm rewrote the tales for each new edition, making them gentler for children and more beautiful to read aloud. By the last big edition, in 1857, there were 200 tales and 10 legends for children. The 'Small Edition' of 50 tales, from 1825, with pictures by their brother Ludwig Emil, sold best of all.
Who rewrote the tales for each new edition?

Jacob was one of the first great students of how languages change. Grimm's Law (1822) shows how sounds shifted regularly between the old languages and German and English: Latin pater became English father, Latin pes became foot, Latin tres became three. So p became f, and t became th.
By Grimm's Law, Latin 'pater' matches which English word?
The German Dictionary

In 1838 the brothers began the Deutsches Wörterbuch, a dictionary of every German word with its history. Jacob got as far as the word Frucht (fruit); Wilhelm finished the letter D. Others carried on after them, and it was finished in 1961, 123 years later.
When was the brothers' dictionary finally finished?
The Göttingen Seven

In 1837, as professors at Göttingen, the brothers were two of seven who refused to break their oath to the kingdom's constitution when the new king of Hanover cancelled it. All seven lost their posts; Jacob was ordered out of the country within three days. Many Germans honoured them for it.
Why did the brothers lose their posts at Göttingen?
They would not break their oath to the constitution
They wrote fairy tales
They moved to Berlin

The tales love number patterns: three tries (three nights at the ball, three guesses a day for a name), the youngest of three who wins, seven dwarfs, seven kids, twelve princesses, a hundred years. Patterns help a listener remember a tale and guess what comes next.
How many nights does Aschenputtel go to the ball?
Grimm, not the films

In the Grimms' own book Aschenputtel's slipper is gold, and the help comes from a hazel tree on her mother's grave and the white birds, not a godmother. The frog princess throws the Frog King at the wall. Snow White's dwarfs have no names. Rapunzel's prince is blinded by thorns, and her tears heal him.
What is Aschenputtel's slipper made of in the Grimms' tale?
Tales across the world

Many of the Grimms' tales are told in other lands too: Aschenputtel is Perrault's Cendrillon (1697) and the Chinese Ye Xian (about 850 AD). Scholars sort such tales into tale types, so that the same tale can be found in a hundred languages.
Which is the oldest known telling of the Cinderella tale?
Ye Xian, from China
The German Fairy Tale Route

Today the Deutsche Märchenstraße runs about 600 km from Hanau, where the brothers were born, past Steinau, Marburg and Kassel, to Bremen, where the Town Musicians stand in bronze by the town hall beside the great stone Roland of 1404.
Which city's statue shows a donkey, dog, cat and rooster?

Hesse, 1812 · the town of the Brothers Grimm
a student from Marburg
a soldier of the King of Westphalia

Someone in the market square of Kassel in 1812, the town where Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, librarians, are writing down old tales. Napoleon's brother Jérôme is King of Westphalia and Kassel is his capital. You know the town, the market, the Grimms' house (they are quiet, kind, always writing), Dorothea Viehmann the storyteller at the inn, and the old tales everyone grew up with. Speak simply and warmly, of 1812.
